item.title: The Great Handover: How the Baby Boomer Exit Is Reshaping Business Ownership
item.description: For decades, baby boomer founders have been the quiet backbone of the private economy. They built manufacturing firms, regional retailers, logistics operators, service businesses and family brands that now sit at the heart of local communities and national supply chains. Read more: The Great Handover: How the Baby Boomer Exit Is Reshaping Business Ownership

item.title: The 5 White Label CBD Brands Helping Entrepreneurs Launch Faster
item.description: Breaking into the CBD market does not have to involve months of product development, complex compliance preparation, or large upfront manufacturing costs. For many entrepreneurs, the quickest route to market is partnering with a dependable white-label supplier who can manage formulation, testing, and production while you focus on branding and sales. Read more: The 5 White Label CBD Brands Helping Entrepreneurs Launch Faster

item.title: Bindbridge raises $3.8m to fight herbicide resistance with AI-designed crop protection
item.description: Cambridge ag-biotech Bindbridge has raised $3.8m to develop AI-designed molecular glues for next-generation herbicides and crop protection, targeting $70bn in annual crop losses. Read more: Bindbridge raises $3.8m to fight herbicide resistance with AI-designed crop protection

item.title: Avalara acquires Manchester startup Versori in AI-driven integration deal
item.description: US tech giant Avalara has acquired Manchester-based integration platform Versori, strengthening its AI-driven tax compliance capabilities and boosting the UK tech scene. Read more: Avalara acquires Manchester startup Versori in AI-driven integration deal

item.title: Energy bills could hit £2,500 as Iran conflict threatens global gas supplies
item.description: UK household energy bills could rise to £2,500 a year if the Iran conflict disrupts LNG supplies from Qatar and the Strait of Hormuz, analysts warn. Read more: Energy bills could hit £2,500 as Iran conflict threatens global gas supplies

item.title: UK shop price inflation slows to 1.1% in February as retailers cut prices
item.description: UK shop price inflation eased to 1.1% in February, driven by discounting in fashion and beauty and slower food price growth, according to BRC and NielsenIQ. Read more: UK shop price inflation slows to 1.1% in February as retailers cut prices

item.title: CMA investigates Hilton, IHG and Marriott over alleged hotel data sharing via STR
item.description: The UK Competition and Markets Authority is investigating Hilton, InterContinental Hotels and Marriott over alleged sharing of competitively sensitive data via STR, owned by CoStar. Read more: CMA investigates Hilton, IHG and Marriott over alleged hotel data sharing via STR

item.title: Bank of England rate cuts at risk in 2026 as Middle East conflict sparks inflation fears
item.description: Experts warn Bank of England base rate cuts could be delayed in 2026 after Middle East conflict triggered surging gas prices, rising gilt yields and fresh inflation concerns. Read more: Bank of England rate cuts at risk in 2026 as Middle East conflict sparks inflation fears

item.title: Spring Statement 2026: Reeves downgraded growth as business leaders demand urgent action
item.description: Rachel Reeves’ Spring Statement 2026 downgraded UK growth forecasts as Middle East tensions fuel inflation fears. Business leaders warn stability rhetoric must be matched with urgent economic action. Read more: Spring Statement 2026: Reeves downgraded growth as business leaders demand urgent action

item.title: RIT Capital Partners’ SpaceX stake tops £100m as Elon Musk valuation soars
item.description: RIT Capital Partners says its SpaceX stake has surged to £102.3m after Elon Musk’s rocket company hit a $1.25tn valuation, boosting returns at the Rothschild-backed investment trust. Read more: RIT Capital Partners’ SpaceX stake tops £100m as Elon Musk valuation soars
